0.content:
Neuvillette is the Hydro Dragon, one of the Seven Sovereigns who ruled the elements before the Heavenly Principles came. Those "usurpers" took the dragons' authority and gave it to The Seven; his was locked in the Hydro Archon's divine throne. He was born in human form, with most of his memories and power lost, not knowing why. In 4.1, when sudden rain fell after the Primordial Sea broke into the Fortress of Meropide, the Traveler guessed the truth. He confirmed it and asked them to keep it secret. When the throne was destroyed in 4.2, he "reforged the throne and title of a Fully Fledged Dragon".

He calls the Heavenly Principles "a cluster of filthy feathers" ruling a world that once belonged to "the Formidable Father" (Nibelung). His character story also says he is "the destroyer of the present order, the one who shall judge all gods, and the foe of humanity". In practice he has pardoned humanity and lives among it. He was told he should care for Fontainians because they too were born from the Primordial Sea, and he will not admit how fascinated by human joys and sorrows he has become. He wonders whether Nibelung was wrong, and whether the Abyss can only be opposed if all life works together.

1.comment: Neuvillette: Focalors, Furina and the Seat in the Theater
1.content:
Focalors invited Neuvillette to Fontaine with a letter and, he later learned, arranged for him to be Iudex so that living among humans would teach him to feel as they do. For five centuries she hid inside the Oratrice, storing up Indemnitium, while her human half Furina played the Hydro Archon without knowing the plan. In 4.2 Neuvillette put Furina on trial and found her guilty; the Oratrice then sentenced "the Hydro Archon" to death. In a vision Focalors explained everything: the sentence would destroy the divine throne and return his authority. "Hydro Dragon, Hydro Dragon, don't cry," she teased. She was executed, and he declared, "People of Fontaine, your sins are forgiven."

He told Furina everything Focalors had said. She replied that she was tired, gave up the Archon's post, left its affairs to him and moved out of the opera house like an ordinary person. He makes sure she lacks nothing, and is "somewhat happy for her". He says that, though meek and full of doubt, she "used madness to stiffen her resolve", and promises to attend in person and applaud if she ever returns to the stage. He lent her the Opera Epiclese for a troupe's final play.

2.content:
Neuvillette brought Melusines, whom many Fontainians once saw as omens of calamity, into society and the Marechaussee Phantom, and contributed this article to the legal code: "A Melusine shall be addressed as 'she,' rather than 'it,' for they are people too." To them he is the ideal father. Asked why the dragon gave them human rights, he says, "It wasn't up to me. Melusines simply prefer being around humans, that's all." Melusines staff the Palais Mermonia, including his aide Sedene.

Sigewinne, head nurse at the Fortress of Meropide, is especially dear to him. He wonders how she is, wants to know when her next vacation is, and would summon Wriothesley to explain any rumour of her being bullied. Years ago she drank a potion left by her dying teacher and took a human form so she could cure a sick human girl, her first patient, breaking an ancient law, and confessed it to him herself. He passed sentence. Later he concluded the law was probably Egeria's way of hiding the truth from her people, and he regrets how ruthless the law could be.

3.content:
A little over four hundred years ago, the new Iudex began reforms and brought Melusines, including Carole, to the Court at their request. His two most trusted subordinates were Carole and Vautrin, head of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol. Conservatives who opposed the reforms used Carole's identity to stir up unrest and force him to give up power. Carole took her own life to prove her innocence, and Vautrin took revenge on those responsible. Neuvillette sentenced him to the Fortress of Meropide. Ever since, he has handled Melusine cases with special care.

In the Diluvies Chapter (4.1), a threat against the young Melusine Kiara, who came to the Court with Carole long ago, made him investigate personally with the Traveler. The culprit, Domenico, was seeking revenge on him. Wriothesley reminded him that today's Fontainians are not those of the past. Walking in a sudden downpour, he felt the memories of five centuries in the rain, Carole and Vautrin among them.

4.content:
Callas, founder of the Spina di Rosula, was framed for murder and died in a court duel against Clorinde. Neuvillette suspected his innocence but did not stop the duel, expecting Callas to yield. In 4.0 he apologised to Navia, who rejected him as insincere, and it rained as she left. They have since exchanged apologies, but he still feels "very distant from her, as if I'm observing the starry sky from the bottom of a deep lake", and knows it cannot easily be mended.

Navia nevertheless works with him: she helped stage Furina's trial, and he rescued her consciousness from a mock trial held by the Primordial Sea's victims when she fell into Primordial water.

5.content:
He met the Traveler as a defence advocate in Lyney's trial (4.0) and came to rely on them as someone with no ties to Fontaine's factions. In 4.2 he made them his "executor" in place of the broken Oratrice and shared the ancient dragons' power with them to defeat the All-Devouring Narwhal. He invites them, as one "from beyond the stars", to witness his judgment of "this upended world" and says travelling with them changed his views.

After the Narwhal, the Traveler told him they were the fourth Descender. He was intrigued and wondered whether their body has properties like the Gnoses. He warned them about Capitano before Natlan and said Fontaine's doors would always be open. In 4.1 he sent them into the Fortress by having them eat a slice of cake meant for the Archon, then charged them with eating it, earning them a 45-day sentence. He can hear Paimon's whispers.

6.content: Neuvillette sentenced the young Wriothesley for killing his adoptive parents, then later fought hard for the title and reputation Wriothesley now has as administrator of the Fortress of Meropide. He will not say why. The Fortress lies outside the court's jurisdiction, and he respects that line, as he told the Knave in 4.1. They sealed the sluice gate together in the Primordial Sea crisis and share a running joke with Clorinde about a stone legal codex. Clorinde, the Champion Duelist, is a successor of the Marechaussee Hunters and essential to the court's fairness.

7.comment: Neuvillette: The Hydro Gnosis, Skirk and the Knave
7.content: After Focalors's divinity faded, she handed him the Hydro Gnosis. Skirk, Childe's master, sensed it and called it the "remains of the Third Descender", advising him to get rid of such "objects of misfortune". She promised to ask her own master about the Third Descender and send word through her disciple. With the throne gone and the Oratrice stopped, he decided the Gnosis meant nothing for Fontaine and gave it to Arlecchino as a "diplomatic gift" for the Fatui's help during the crisis, to avoid needless conflict. The Gnosis passed into Fatui hands.

8.content: Neuvillette is a self-proclaimed connoisseur of Teyvat's natural waters. Mondstadt's water is crisp and pure, Liyue's has an enduring aftertaste, Inazuma's has unmatched depth, and Sumeru's is complex and must be savoured patiently. Pyro-heated water tastes "au naturel", charcoal-boiled water rustic, and melted Snezhnayan river ice nothing like Cryo-chilled water. He rarely leaves Fontaine, so he has spring water delivered, and he can tell the samples apart. Privately he cannot see why Fonta is popular, though he admits it rehydrates and restores blood sugar cheaply. He likes dishes with plenty of liquid and calls Charcoal-Baked Ajilenakh Cake harder on the stomach than a dehumidifying agent.

9.comment: Neuvillette: The Judgment of The Seven
9.content: Neuvillette has vowed to judge each of The Seven in turn, "even if the sky should fall and the ground give way", because each holds an Authority taken from the dragons. His final destiny, he says, is to judge the Usurper-King in the heavens. He is in no hurry: he means to stay in Fontaine perhaps another four hundred years, and a trial need not lead to a fight. He promises the common folk will not be harmed. "They owe a debt of blood that shall not be forgotten."
